title: RecoveryLab scenario
description: One request, the state that shows its effect, and the failure to inject. See https://github.com/Wali05/recoverylab#write-a-scenario-by-hand

name.description: Shown in reports. Defaults to the file name.

scenario.description: Which failure `run` injects. `audit` ignores this and runs every scenario that applies.

timeout.description: Deadline for the whole experiment. Default 20s.

concurrency.description: Copies sent at once by concurrent-duplicates. Default 16.

service.description: A foreground process RecoveryLab starts, and kills for crash-after-ack.

command.description: The server executable and its arguments, with no shell wrapper.

working_dir.description: Relative to the scenario file. Default: the scenario file's folder.

ready_url.description: Returns 2xx once the service is ready.

request.description: The write being tested. {{run_id}} is replaced with a fresh value per run.

body.description: Any JSON value, sent as the request body.

changed_body.description: key-reuse only: the body sent with the reused key. Must differ from request.body by value.

checks.description: Several named state checks. Use instead of observe.

retry_response.description: lost-response and crash-after-ack: what the retry must return. Without it, a lost-response retry must be 2xx.

same_json_pointers.description: Values that must match between the original reply and the retry, such as /order_id.

concurrent_response.description: concurrent-duplicates: HTTP codes the burst may return, such as [201, 409].

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON pointer, such as /count. Empty means the whole document.

url.description: A GET endpoint whose response shows the effect.

measure.description: value reads an integer; length counts the items in an array.

expected_delta.description: How much one successful write should change the value, such as 1, or -1 for a delete.
